rows.annotation: Putative laminin-binding outer membrane adhesin (DUF1302 family).
rows.evidence: PA3923, a 47.7%-identical homolog, binds laminin directly (KD 6.9 nM) and supports adhesion and biofilm formation on laminin-coated surfaces. Curated homologs at 48.0–48.4% identity are annotated as putative DUF1302 adhesins. The query has a nearly full-length DUF1302 domain and a predicted outer membrane beta-barrel with a cleavable signal peptide. Laminin specificity remains untested in the query, warranting 'putative'; detergent fitness defects support a surface-associated role without establishing transport activity.
rows.reasoning_trace: Tier A is supported by direct biochemical characterization of laminin binding in the 47.7%-identical PA3923 homolog. Homolog experiments, curated adhesin annotations, query DUF1302 and topology predictions, fitness, cofitness, neighborhood, and STRING evidence are available; cofitness is weak and neighborhood does not establish a specific mechanism. A specific OmpC/OmpF/PhoE porin assignment is rejected because the STRING orthogroup label is less functionally discriminating than the characterized adhesin homolog and does not establish channel activity.

Evidence type: experimental
PA3923 is identified as a high-affinity laminin receptor located in the outer membrane of P. aeruginosa [FIG:Fig2]. Transposon mutants lacking PA3923 exhibit significantly reduced adherence to immobilized laminin-111 compared to the wild-type PAO1 strain [FIG:Fig3]. Recombinant PA3923 binds laminin in a dose-dependent manner with a dissociation constant (KD) of 6.9 nM [FIG:Fig4]. TEM imaging shows that PA3923 adheres to the LG domains at the tips of the laminin molecule [FIG:Fig5], specifically binding to LG5 and LG4 [FIG:Fig6]. This interaction is inhibited by heparan sulphate, indicating the involvement of heparin-binding domains [FIG:Fig6].
[[END SUMMARY]]
[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 47.70
Homolog originates from: Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1
Evidence type: experimental
This gene encodes a hypothetical protein that was found to be frequently differentially expressed and co-regulated with biofilm-related genes in a transcriptomic compendium. Correlation analysis with laminin-binding proteins and pathway enrichment analysis predicted its role in biofilm formation. Biofilm assays using transposon insertion mutants (PA3923::TnM_1 and PA3923::TnM_2) demonstrated a significant reduction in biofilm formation on laminin-coated surfaces compared to wild-type PA14 without affecting planktonic growth (Fig 6).

rows.topology_evidence:
[[BEGIN MEMBRANE TOPOLOGY PREDICTION]]
Predicted by DeepTMHMM 1.0 on the QUERY sequence itself (not on a homolog).
Predicted class: BETA
Signal peptide: residues 1-27 (cleavable)
Membrane-spanning BETA strands: 18 (a beta-barrel of 18 strands)
  strand positions: 39-50, 77-89, 96-104, 132-140, 150-162, 195-203, 210-217, 288-294, 303-310, 379-385, 392-398, 449-456, 468-475, 528-537, 546-554, 572-580, 586-595, 607-615
Meaning: the protein forms a BETA-BARREL that spans the OUTER MEMBRANE. In Gram-negative bacteria beta-barrel proteins are outer membrane proteins (OMPs). This is a positive outer-membrane call, not merely an export call. It is NOT an inner-membrane protein: those use alpha-helical transmembrane segments, and this protein has none.
[[END MEMBRANE TOPOLOGY PREDICTION]]
rows.conservation_breadth:
[[BEGIN CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
Counted over EVERY homolog found for this query, before the per-source display caps that apply to the other evidence blocks.
Distinct organisms with a homolog: 19 (in 4 genera)
Query organism: Pseudomonas putida
Organisms OTHER than the query's own with a homolog: 18 (3 genera other than Pseudomonas)
%Identity to query across these homologs: 30.3-98.9
Meaning: breadth of conservation, not function. A homolog in an organism other than the query's own is evidence the protein is real and under selection even when no function can be named, and supports calling it a CONSERVED hypothetical protein; homologs confined to the query's own organism do not. More organisms and more genera mean broader conservation. This NEVER constrains the specific function.
[[END CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
